correctness.rationale: The 16 exceptional lines have a triangle-free 40-edge intersection graph, so every rational divisor point is either on a rational component (with inclusion-exclusion of intersections) or the intersection of two Frobenius-interchanged components. This proves \(\#D=m(q+1)-a+b\). The rank-six Picard trace gives \(\#X=q^2+\tau q+1\) and hence the extension-field formula. The signed edge representation has character a-b and yields the zeta determinant identity by the trace-log determinant formula. All 1920 signed permutations and their 18 conjugacy classes were enumerated in executable exact standard-library code, returning 15 profiles and 14 polynomials. An independent projective-plane enumeration reproduced the known split cases for six prime fields and the new nonsplit coordinate-transposition profile for four prime fields, using exact quadratic extensions. The theorem does not assert finite-field realization of every abstract W(D5) element.

value.rationale: The all-exceptional-curve complement is an intrinsic arithmetic open variety. Its complete field-extension point counts and zeta are natural invariants distinct from the closed surface trace. The classification distinguishes several incidence types with identical Picard trace, organizes all 1920 Weyl actions into fifteen profiles, and gives exact full-zeta data rather than a lone small-field experiment. The historically known split formula is only a reference and not the contribution. Independent nonsplit geometric tests substantiate that the classification distinguishes more than the classical split value.
